from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Classical searching checks unsorted items one by one.",
            "A million boxes might require half a million checks.",
            "Grover’s Algorithm finds the answer much faster.",
            "It needs only one thousand steps for that million.",
            "This is a massive quadratic speedup for searching."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Classical vs. Quantum Search Problem", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        box_color = "#FFFFFF"
        scan_color = "#00FF00"
        star_color = "#FFD700"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display four white boxes (#FFFFFF) labeled 1 to 4 in a row.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(box_color))
        
        boxes = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 5):
            sq = Square(side_length=0.8, color=box_color)
            lbl = Text(str(i), font_size=24, color=box_color)
            box = VGroup(sq, lbl)
            self.place_at_grid(box, f"B{i+1}")
            boxes.add(box)
            
        self.play(Create(boxes))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # A green circle (#00FF00) scans boxes 1, 2, and 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(scan_color)
        )
        
        scanner = Circle(radius=0.15, color=scan_color, fill_opacity=1)
        # Start at Box 1
        self.place_at_grid(scanner, "B2")
        self.play(FadeIn(scanner))
        # Move scanner over Box 1 to Box 2
        self.play(scanner.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # box 3 opens to reveal a gold star (#FFD700).
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(star_color)
        )
        
        star = Star(n=5, outer_radius=0.3, color=star_color, fill_opacity=1)
        self.place_at_grid(star, "B4")
        
        # Scan to Box 3 and reveal star
        self.play(scanner.animate.move_to(self.grid["B4"]))
        self.play(
            boxes[2][1].animate.set_opacity(0), # Hide label '3'
            FadeIn(star)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Display comparison text: 'Classical: O(N)' vs 'Quantum: O(sqrt(N))'
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(box_color)
        )
        
        comparison_c = Text("Classical: O(N)", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        comparison_q = Text("Quantum: O(sqrt(N))", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        self.place_at_grid(comparison_c, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(comparison_q, "E3")
        
        self.play(Write(comparison_c))
        self.play(Write(comparison_q))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Summary of the speedup
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        speedup_label = Text("Quadratic Speedup", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(speedup_label, "F2", "F5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(speedup_label))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset color
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Prerequisite: The Qubit and Superposition"
        lines = [
            "A qubit is the quantum version of a bit.",
            "It exists in a superposition of two states simultaneously.",
            "We visualize this as a vector in 2D space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        axis_color = "#FFFFFF"
        label0_color = "#00BFFF"
        label1_color = "#FF6347"
        vector_color = "#FFFF00"
        equation_color = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Draw white axes
        origin = self.grid["E2"]
        x_end = self.grid["E6"]
        y_end = self.grid["A2"]
        
        axis_x = Arrow(origin, x_end, color=axis_color, buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        axis_y = Arrow(origin, y_end, color=axis_color, buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError for 'latex'
        label_0 = Text("|0⟩", color=label0_color, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_0, "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        label_1 = Text("|1⟩", color=label1_color, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_1, "A1", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(axis_x), Create(axis_y))
        self.play(Write(label_0), Write(label_1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create a unit vector
        vec_len = np.linalg.norm(self.grid["E6"] - origin)
        # Vector points to |0> initially
        psi_vector = Arrow(origin, origin + RIGHT * vec_len, color=vector_color, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        # Sweeping animation
        self.play(Create(psi_vector))
        
        # Rotate from |0> towards |1> (90 degrees)
        self.play(
            Rotate(psi_vector, angle=PI/2, about_point=origin, rate_func=smooth),
            run_time=2
        )
        # Rotate back to a middle state (superposition)
        self.play(
            Rotate(psi_vector, angle=-PI/4, about_point=origin, rate_func=smooth),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Fixed: Replaced MathTex with Text using unicode characters for math
        equation = Text("|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩", color=equation_color, font_size=24)
        self.place_in_area(equation, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(2)

        # Reset final line color
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "State Vectors and Probability Amplitudes"
        lines = [
            "Vector projections onto the axes are called amplitudes.",
            "Squaring an amplitude reveals the probability of that state.",
            "Measurement collapses the vector into a single result."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # Setup Coordinate System (Axes)
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 1.2, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.2, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE},
            tips=True
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E4")
        
        # Labels for axes - Using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        label_0 = Text("|0⟩", font_size=24).next_to(axes.c2p(1.1, 0), DOWN)
        label_1 = Text("|1⟩", font_size=24).next_to(axes.c2p(0, 1.1), LEFT)
        
        # Yellow state vector at 45 degrees
        vec_end = axes.c2p(np.cos(PI/4), np.sin(PI/4))
        state_vec = Arrow(axes.c2p(0,0), vec_end, buff=0, color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=4)
        
        # Projections
        proj_x = DashedLine(vec_end, axes.c2p(np.cos(PI/4), 0), color=WHITE)
        proj_y = DashedLine(vec_end, axes.c2p(0, np.sin(PI/4)), color=WHITE)
        
        # Amplitude labels α and β - Using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        alpha_label = Text("α", color=WHITE, font_size=30)
        beta_label = Text("β", color=WHITE, font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(alpha_label, "E3", scale_factor=0.8) # Below projection on X
        self.place_at_grid(beta_label, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)  # Left of projection on Y
        
        # Adjusting label positions manually relative to axes since grid is coarse
        alpha_label.move_to(axes.c2p(0.35, -0.2))
        beta_label.move_to(axes.c2p(-0.2, 0.35))

        self.play(Create(axes), Write(label_0), Write(label_1))
        self.play(GrowArrow(state_vec))
        self.play(Create(proj_x), Create(proj_y))
        self.play(Write(alpha_label), Write(beta_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # Probability calculations - Using Text to avoid LaTeX dependency
        prob_alpha = Text("|α|² = 0.5", color="#00FF00", font_size=32)
        prob_beta = Text("|β|² = 0.5", color="#00FF00", font_size=32)
        
        self.place_at_grid(prob_alpha, "B5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_beta, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Write(prob_alpha), Write(prob_beta))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight Line 3
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#58ACFA"))

        # Measurement collapse: Snap to |0>
        # Define the collapsed vector
        collapsed_vec = Arrow(axes.c2p(0,0), axes.c2p(1,0), buff=0, color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=6)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(proj_x),
            FadeOut(proj_y),
            FadeOut(alpha_label),
            FadeOut(beta_label),
            Transform(state_vec, collapsed_vec),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        
        # Final label for collapse result
        result_text = Text("Result: |0⟩", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(result_text, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(result_text))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        title = "Grover's Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)"
        lines = [
            "The Oracle marks the target by flipping its sign.",
            "It reflects the target's amplitude across the axis.",
            "Only the target state becomes negative.",
            "This process is called phase inversion.",
            "It highlights the answer without changing its probability."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependencies
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        
        bars = VGroup()
        labels = VGroup()
        # Changed to text-compatible representation of ket states
        states = ["|00>", "|01>", "|10>", "|11>"]
        
        for i, col_idx in enumerate(["2", "3", "4", "5"]):
            # Height 2.0 centered at Row C makes bottom touch Row D (baseline)
            bar = Rectangle(
                height=2.0, 
                width=0.6, 
                fill_opacity=1.0, 
                fill_color="#00BFFF", 
                stroke_color="#00BFFF"
            )
            self.place_at_grid(bar, f"C{col_idx}")
            bars.add(bar)
            
            # Labels at top (Row A) - Using Text to avoid "latex not found" error
            label = Text(states[i], font_size=24, color=WHITE)
            self.place_at_grid(label, f"A{col_idx}")
            labels.add(label)
            
        self.play(Create(bars), Write(labels))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Label the third bar as the target state with a gold outline (#FFD700).
        # Draw a white horizontal line (#FFFFFF) representing the zero-amplitude baseline.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        baseline = Line(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["D6"], color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=4)
        # Target bar is index 2
        target_outline = SurroundingRectangle(bars[2], color="#FFD700", buff=0.1, stroke_width=5)
        
        self.play(Create(baseline), Create(target_outline))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Only the target state becomes negative.
        # The Oracle reflects the target bar below the axis, changing its color to tomato (#FF6347).
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        
        # Move target bar from C4 to E4 (perfect reflection across D4)
        self.play(
            bars[2].animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]).set_color("#FF6347"),
            target_outline.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # This process is called phase inversion.
        # Flash the negative tomato bar (#FF6347) once to emphasize the phase flip.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.play(Flash(bars[2], color="#FF6347", line_length=0.4, flash_radius=0.6))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # It highlights the answer without changing its probability.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Emphasize the highlighted state
        self.play(
            target_outline.animate.set_stroke(width=10),
            bars[2].animate.set_opacity(0.7),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            target_outline.animate.set_stroke(width=5),
            bars[2].animate.set_opacity(1.0),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lecture_lines_text = [
            "The Diffusion Operator performs inversion about the mean.",
            "First, it calculates the average of all amplitudes.",
            "Then, it reflects every amplitude across that average level.",
            "The negative target amplitude is boosted significantly.",
            "This trampoline effect amplifies the correct answer's probability."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Grover's Step 2: The Diffusion Operator", lecture_lines_text)

        # Colors
        CYAN_C = "#00BFFF"
        TOMATO_C = "#FF6347"
        GOLD_C = "#FFD700"
        WHITE_C = "#FFFFFF"

        # Constants for Bar Chart
        bar_width = 0.6
        initial_heights = [1.0, 1.0, -1.0, 1.0] # Representing 0.5, 0.5, -0.5, 0.5 amplitudes
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(CYAN_C)
        
        # Create bars and baseline
        baseline = Line(start=np.array([-2, 0, 0]), end=np.array([2, 0, 0]), color=GREY_E)
        
        bars = VGroup()
        for i, h in enumerate(initial_heights):
            color = CYAN_C if h > 0 else TOMATO_C
            # Rectangle(width, height) centers the rect. We want bottom-aligned for positive, top-aligned for negative.
            # So we create a rect and shift it.
            rect = Rectangle(width=bar_width, height=abs(h), fill_color=color, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=2)
            if h > 0:
                rect.next_to(baseline.point_from_proportion(0.2 + 0.2 * i), UP, buff=0)
            else:
                rect.next_to(baseline.point_from_proportion(0.2 + 0.2 * i), DOWN, buff=0)
            bars.add(rect)

        chart_group = VGroup(baseline, bars)
        self.place_in_area(chart_group, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(baseline), Create(bars))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE_C)
        
        # Calculate mean
        mean_h = sum(initial_heights) / len(initial_heights) # (1+1-1+1)/4 = 0.5
        # The baseline is at some y. The mean line is relative to baseline.
        mean_y = baseline.get_y() + mean_h * (bars[0].height / abs(initial_heights[0]))
        
        mean_line = DashedLine(
            start=baseline.get_left() + UP * (mean_h * 0.5 * bars[0].height / abs(initial_heights[0])),
            end=baseline.get_right() + UP * (mean_h * 0.5 * bars[0].height / abs(initial_heights[0])),
            color=WHITE_C
        )
        # Note: height scaling factor correction. bars[0].height corresponds to |initial_heights[0]|.
        # Let's fix the position
        mean_line.move_to(baseline.get_center() + UP * (mean_h * (bars[0].height / abs(initial_heights[0]))))
        
        mean_label = Text("Mean", font_size=16, color=WHITE_C).next_to(mean_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(mean_line), Write(mean_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE_C)
        
        # New heights: 2*mean - old_height
        # 2*0.5 - 1.0 = 0
        # 2*0.5 - (-1.0) = 2.0
        target_heights = [2*mean_h - h for h in initial_heights]
        
        # Animate reflection
        animations = []
        for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
            new_h = target_heights[i]
            # Handle the transition
            if abs(new_h) < 0.05: # Effectively zero
                animations.append(bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.01).move_to(baseline.point_from_proportion(0.2 + 0.2 * i)))
            else:
                # Calculate the new bar
                new_bar_height = abs(new_h) * (bars[0].height / abs(initial_heights[0]))
                # We need to stretch and shift so it remains aligned to baseline
                if new_h > 0:
                    animations.append(bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(new_bar_height).next_to(baseline.point_from_proportion(0.2 + 0.2 * i), UP, buff=0))
                else:
                    animations.append(bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(new_bar_height).next_to(baseline.point_from_proportion(0.2 + 0.2 * i), DOWN, buff=0))

        self.play(*animations, run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GOLD_C)
        
        # Target bar (index 2) turns gold
        self.play(bars[2].animate.set_fill(GOLD_C), bars[2].animate.set_stroke(GOLD_C))
        
        # Show magnitude increase indicator
        arrow = Arrow(start=mean_line.get_center() + DOWN*0.5, end=bars[2].get_top(), color=GOLD_C, buff=0.1)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(CYAN_C)
        
        # Non-target bars shrink towards zero if they haven't already
        shrink_anims = []
        for i in [0, 1, 3]:
            shrink_anims.append(bars[i].animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.001).move_to(baseline.point_from_proportion(0.2 + 0.2 * i)))
        
        self.play(*shrink_anims, FadeOut(arrow), FadeOut(mean_line), FadeOut(mean_label))
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            "Repeating these steps makes the target state dominate.",
            "The correct answer reaches nearly 100% probability.",
            "We then measure the system to find our item."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Measurement and Convergence", lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Symbols for Oracle and Diffusion
        oracle_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=WHITE)
        oracle_text = Text("Oracle", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        oracle_group = VGroup(oracle_box, oracle_text)
        
        diffusion_box = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=WHITE)
        diffusion_text = Text("Diffusion", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        diffusion_group = VGroup(diffusion_box, diffusion_text)
        
        self.place_at_grid(oracle_group, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(diffusion_group, "D3")
        
        # Repeat loop symbol
        loop_arrow = CurvedArrow(
            self.grid["D4"] + RIGHT*0.5, 
            self.grid["B4"] + RIGHT*0.5, 
            angle=-PI, 
            color=WHITE
        )
        loop_label = Text("Repeat", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(loop_label, "C5")
        
        self.play(Create(oracle_group), Create(diffusion_group))
        self.play(Create(loop_arrow), Write(loop_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeOut(oracle_group), FadeOut(diffusion_group), FadeOut(loop_arrow), FadeOut(loop_label))
        
        # Bar Chart representation
        # 4 bars, index 2 is target
        bar_width = 0.6
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=bar_width, height=0.5, fill_opacity=0.6, color=BLUE_E)
            for _ in range(4)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # Highlight target bar in GOLD
        bars[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        bars[2].set_fill("#FFD700", opacity=0.8)
        
        self.place_in_area(bars, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(bars))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Convergence animation: target grows, others vanish
        self.play(
            bars[2].animate.stretch_to_fit_height(4).move_to(bars[2].get_bottom() + UP*2),
            bars[0].animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.05).move_to(bars[0].get_bottom() + UP*0.025),
            bars[1].animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.05).move_to(bars[1].get_bottom() + UP*0.025),
            bars[3].animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.05).move_to(bars[3].get_bottom() + UP*0.025),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Reveal Pixel star and Search Complete text
        pixel_star = Star(color="#FFD700", fill_opacity=1.0).scale(0.8)
        complete_text = Text("Search Complete", font_size=32, color="#FFFFFF")
        
        self.place_at_grid(pixel_star, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(complete_text, "E3")
        
        self.play(FadeOut(bars))
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(pixel_star))
        self.play(Write(complete_text))
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Quantum Search: From Qubits to Grover's Algorithm
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or technology enthusiasts with basic linear algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Search Problem
sections.content: Introduce the inefficiency of classical searching in unstructured data. Explain that while a classical computer checks items one-by-one (O(N)), a quantum computer uses Grover's Algorithm to find the answer in O(√N) steps.
sections.example: A cat named 'Pixel' is hiding in one of 4 closed boxes. A classical robot must open them one by one. If there are 1,000,000 boxes, the robot takes 500,000 tries on average; Grover's algorithm only needs about 1,000.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Qubit and Superposition
sections.content: Define the Qubit as the fundamental unit. Explain superposition using a 2D coordinate system where the state is a unit vector. Introduce the Bra-Ket notation |0⟩ and |1⟩ as the axes of this space.
sections.example: Visualizing a spinning coin: while spinning, it is not 'Heads' (|0⟩) or 'Tails' (|1⟩), but a vector |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩, existing in both states simultaneously.

sections.title: State Vectors and Probability Amplitudes
sections.content: Explain that the 'length' of the vector projections (α and β) onto the axes are amplitudes. The square of these amplitudes determines the probability of finding the system in that state upon measurement. Use a circle graph to show how the vector rotates.
sections.example: If the state vector is tilted 45 degrees between |0⟩ and |1⟩, the amplitudes are equal (1/√2). Squaring them gives a 50/50 chance of finding the cat in either state.

sections.title: Grover's Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
sections.content: Introduce the 'Oracle' as a mathematical function that 'marks' the correct answer by flipping its sign (phase). Graphically, this reflects the state vector of the correct answer across the horizontal axis, making its amplitude negative.
sections.example: Imagine four bars representing the probability amplitudes of four boxes. The Oracle acts like a 'marker' that flips the bar of the box containing 'Pixel' upside down, while leaving others untouched.

sections.title: Grover's Step 2: The Diffusion Operator
sections.content: Explain 'Inversion about the Mean.' This mathematical operation calculates the average amplitude of all states and reflects all amplitudes across that average. This causes the 'marked' (negative) state to grow significantly while others shrink.
sections.example: If the 'Pixel' bar is at -0.5 and others are at +0.5, the average is low. Flipping everyone across this average makes the 'Pixel' bar shoot up to nearly 1.0, like a trampoline effect boosting the right answer.

sections.title: Measurement and Convergence
sections.content: Explain that these two steps (Oracle + Diffusion) are repeated until the state vector is almost perfectly aligned with the target state. Conclude with measurement, where the high amplitude collapses into a definite result.
sections.example: After a few 'bounces' of the diffusion trampoline, the probability of box #3 is 99%. We open the box, and there is Pixel the cat! The quantum search is complete.

storyboard.title: The Classical vs. Quantum Search Problem
lecture_lines: Classical searching checks unsorted items one by one.
A million boxes might require half a million checks.
Grover’s Algorithm finds the answer much faster.
It needs only one thousand steps for that million.
This is a massive quadratic speedup for searching.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Qubit and Superposition
lecture_lines: A qubit is the quantum version of a bit.

storyboard.title: State Vectors and Probability Amplitudes
lecture_lines: Vector projections onto the axes are called amplitudes.
Squaring an amplitude reveals the probability of that state.

storyboard.title: Grover's Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
lecture_lines: The Oracle marks the target by flipping its sign.
It reflects the target's amplitude across the axis.
Only the target state becomes negative.
This process is called phase inversion.
It highlights the answer without changing its probability.
animations: Display four cyan bars (#00BFFF) on a white baseline (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Grover's Step 2: The Diffusion Operator
lecture_lines: The Diffusion Operator performs inversion about the mean.
First, it calculates the average of all amplitudes.
Then, it reflects every amplitude across that average level.
The negative target amplitude is boosted significantly.
This trampoline effect amplifies the correct answer's probability.

A dashed white line (#FFFFFF) appears at the average height of all bars.

The target bar grows to maximum height and turns gold (#FFD700).
The three non-target bars shrink towards the zero baseline.

storyboard.title: Measurement and Convergence

The correct answer reaches nearly 100% probability.
We then measure the system to find our item.

The target bar (#FFD700) reaches peak height while others vanish.
